subject: State EDU — request for data flow annex, DPIA excerpts, SCCs status
messages:
From: Frank Jenkins <frank.jenkins@franklinstate.edu>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: susan.kim@franklinstate.edu
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: State EDU procurement request — data flow annex & DPIA excerpts

Good morning Grace,

We're kicking off contract review for a statewide pilot and procurement needs a few pieces from Redwood to complete the packet: specifically a detailed data flow annex that maps how student/educational records traverse your system (ingress, storage, processors, sub-processors, backups), redacted DPIA excerpts showing lawful basis and risk mitigations, and a brief statement of SCCs execution status (are standard contractual clauses in place for any cross-border transfers?).

A few clarifications that will help procurement:
- The pilot will process education records that include student identifiers and limited health-related flags; FERPA and state education privacy rules apply.
- Please identify any third-party analytics or logging that retains PII beyond 30 days.
- Our procurement timeline is tight: committee packet due 20 Aug.

Can you confirm what you can provide by COB next Monday (17 Aug) and whether you can supply a single PDF we can route to our legal team? We may ask for a short cover memo summarizing residual risks for the packet.

Thanks,

Frank Jenkins
IT Director — Franklin State Department of Education
frank.jenkins@franklinstate.edu
(555) 867-1020

Attachment: none
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Frank Jenkins <frank.jenkins@franklinstate.edu>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: State EDU procurement request — data flow annex & DPIA excerpts

Frank — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We're on it. Quick summary of next steps from our side:

1) I'll coordinate delivery of a redacted DPIA summary and a focused data flow annex that highlights where student identifiers are processed and retained.
2) I'll loop in Rishi (security/compliance) and Vivek (legal) to confirm SCCs status and any state-specific audit language.
3) We can produce a single consolidated PDF for procurement and a 1-page cover memo summarizing residual risks and mitigations.

Two quick questions to make sure we tailor the annex properly:
- Can you confirm whether the pilot will include file uploads (parent/teacher documents) or only structured records from the SIS?
- Do you require HIPAA BAA-level controls for the health-related flags, or will FERPA/state rules be the primary concern?

If helpful we can do a 30-minute call Thursday morning to walk procurement through the artifacts before you finalize the packet.

I'll aim to get the initial artifacts to you by EOD Friday (14 Aug) for an internal review, and final consolidated PDF by COB 17 Aug.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Frank Jenkins <frank.jenkins@franklinstate.edu>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: susan.kim@franklinstate.edu
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: State EDU procurement request — data flow annex & DPIA excerpts

Grace — thanks. To clarify: the pilot will ingest structured feeds from the SIS (Student Information System) plus occasional parent-uploaded PDFs (consent forms). The uploads will be scanned for metadata and stored in object storage.

Regarding compliance: FERPA is primary, but some records will include health indicators captured by the SIS. We do not expect PHI-level attachments in the pilot, but we'd like confirmation on logging retention windows and whether Redwood can offer a BAA if needed.

Procurement details: PO/Procurement ID FRD-PO-2026-0785. I've uploaded our procurement packet to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bProcurementFolderExample

We are available for a call Thursday 10:00–11:00 AM ET if that works for your team.

—Frank

Frank — Rishi from Security & Compliance here. Attached are the artifacts we discussed and a short explanation of what each contains. We redacted customer-identifying details and sample data where appropriate.

Attachments (attached to this message):
- RI_DataFlow_Annex_v1.1.pdf — architecture diagram + processing steps (ingest -> staging -> inference -> object store -> backups). The annex highlights retention windows and where PII is pseudonymized.
- DPIA_summary_redacted.pdf — excerpted sections: lawful basis, risk register, mitigation mapping (access controls, encryption, KV cache retention policy).
- SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf — A SOC 2 Type II cover page and control summary (redacted for customer names). This demonstrates logging, incident response, and access review controls.
- SCCs_execution_statement.docx — short memo describing our approach to SCCs: we use EU SCCs where applicable; for transfers to third-party sub-processors we either rely on SCCs or implement equivalent safeguards. Execution of SCCs requires a DPA signature from the controller.

Notes and requests:
- We have a configurable logging retention; default token and access logs are retained 90 days, with an option to reduce retention for sensitive pilots — we can set a 30-day retention for this engagement if required.
- For parent-uploaded PDFs: object retention defaults to 365 days; we can implement policy to purge after X days or move to cold storage with limited access.
- We can provide a BAA for covered PHI scenarios; we'd need to scope which data elements qualify as PHI and confirm the required controls.
- If procurement requires a signed Data Processing Addendum with a state-specific audit clause, please share the exact language. Our legal team (cc'd Vivek) can review and propose redlines.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for Thursday 10:00 AM ET to review the artifacts with your procurement and legal.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Frank Jenkins <frank.jenkins@franklinstate.edu>

Rishi/Grace — thank you for the prompt turnaround and for the artifacts. Procurement asks for one additional item: a short cover letter (1 page) that explains residual risks specific to student data handling and the mitigations we can point to in the packet (retention policy, BAA availability, SCCs status). That letter will be included in the committee packet to summarize why the pilot is approvable.

Also: procurement has a standard state audit clause attached to their template. Can Redwood accept a limited audit right for this pilot (on-site or remote, once per contract year) with reasonable notice? If not, please propose language our legal team can review.

If you can draft the one‑page cover memo and proposed audit language before our 10:00 AM ET call, we can review live.

Appreciate it — look forward to the call.

Frank Jenkins
IT Director — Franklin State Department of Education
